check: the ordering discipline for the closing steps, and the size of what must be preserved
theHazard: Test-S5Release.ps1 passes clean as its first gradle argument, twice. clean deletes the whole build/ tree - including build/run/serverSmoke/vanilla/<runId>/ where the 24h evidence lives, and build/s5-stress-24h2.log. Running it before copying the evidence out destroys the thing the profile was run to produce.

whatIsActuallyAtRisk.samples: 2 MB, irreplaceable - 509 periodic samples plus header.json

thePoint: Almost all of the volume is disposable world data, which is why the directory looks precious and is not. The evidence that matters is about 2 MB, so preserving it costs nothing and losing it costs the run.
correctOrder: 1. Let the profile finish and produce stress-report.json
2. Copy stress-report.json, the samples directory, header.json and build/s5-stress-24h2.log into docs/evidence/ immediately
3. Run gradlew runGameTest, then copy build/reports/gametest/results.xml into docs/evidence/
4. Only then run Test-S5Release.ps1, whose clean may delete everything under build/
5. Update the report, the ledger and the evidence index
whyGameTestAlsoComesFirst: Its results.xml lives in build/reports/gametest and a later build can replace it, so it is copied out in the same pass rather than after.
theGuardOnlyCoversPartOfThis: Test-S5Release refuses to start while a stress profile is running, which stops it deleting a live run. It does not protect a finished run, so ordering is still required.
